correctness.rationale: After affine normalization the local transform is \(P(X,Y)=a+bX+cY+dXY\) on \(\mu_3^2\). In any row, either the affine function of \(Y\) is identically zero or it has at most one zero. Hence without a full zero row there are at most three zeros. If a row \(X=\alpha\) is identically zero, then \(P=(X-\alpha)(b+dY)\), so the zero set is either that row alone (3 zeros) or the union of a full row and a full column (5 zeros). Thus four zeros are impossible. Five explicit all-nonzero coefficient vectors attain zero counts \(0,1,2,3,5\). The actual exact verifier checks those witnesses in \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\) and all 126 four-row constraints, confirming that any all-nonzero rank-three null vector forced by four prescribed zeros actually has five zeros. Multiplying by the ambient fiber count \(3^{d-2}\) proves the result.

value.rationale: This is the smallest ternary two-dimensional affine-parallelogram support problem and gives a complete exact spectrum, including an isolated forbidden intermediate size. It is a natural geometry-sensitive refinement of finite Fourier uncertainty rather than an arbitrary parameter census.
residual_risks: The proof is highly specific to the \(3\times3\) root grid.

final_claim: For every \(d\ge2\), a complex-valued function on \(\mathbb F_3^d\) supported exactly on an affine parallelogram with four nonzero support values has Fourier-support size exactly one of \(\{4,6,7,8,9\}3^{d-2}\), and every listed value occurs; in particular \(5\cdot3^{d-2}\) is impossible.
limitations: Only exact four-point affine-parallelogram supports over \(\mathbb F_3\) are classified.
No assertion is made for other four-point affine types or larger primes.
